name: Grilled Panzanella Salad

ingredients.name: very ripe tomatoes, cut into 1-inch chunks
day-old Italian bread, sliced into 1-inch thick slices

instructions.primary_message: Toss tomato slices with 1/2 teaspoon salt in a large bowl. Set aside at room temperature. Brush zucchini, peppers, red onion, and bread slices with 1/4 cup olive oil and season with salt and pepper.

Ignite 1/2 chimney (2 1/2 quarts) of coals. When coals are mostly covered in gray ash, spread evenly over coal grate. Put cooking grate in place, cover, and preheat for 5 minutes. Scrape grill clean. Place zucchini, peppers, and onions on grate. Cover and cook until first side is lightly charred, about 4 minutes. Flip, cover, and cook until charred on second side and vegetables are tender, about 4 minutes longer (depending on size of vegetables, some may take longer or shorter to cook. Remove from grill as they become tender). Transfer to cutting board and tent loosely with foil.

Meanwhile, grill bread until golden brown on both sides. Transfer to cutting board with vegetables cut bread and vegetables into rough 2.5-cm cubes and transfer to bowl with tomatoes. Add remaining olive oil, vinegar, and parsley. Toss to combine, and season to taste with salt and pepper. Serve immediately. Salad is best eaten within one hour of composing.

description: Charred late-summer vegetables and juicy, ripe tomatoes are tossed with a vinaigrette and hunks of grilled day-old bread, which soaks up all the fabulous juices.
notes: Notes: Use extremely ripe tomatoes, preferably ones that are beginning to split open.
author: J. Kenji López-Alt
